instrumentation_intolerant.note: declared tests bypass the failure-gating comparison only by (script, test) identity — a declaration without script matches only unattributed failures, and same-named tests in undeclared scripts are NOT exempted; they cannot attest behavior under instrumentation, so they are disclosed here and as coverage blind spots — not silently skipped

coverage_semantics.semantics: block-entry hit expands to all statement start lines in the block (line-coverage approximation, not per-statement exact measurement); a runtime error aborting mid-block can mark later statements covered

certification.reason: single round; WP5 owns two-round certification

notes: lanes: test = hits inside a GUT test window (start_test..end_test); script (R1) = hits between start_script and end_script outside any test window (before_all/after_all, inter-test execution); unattributed is subdivided into named phase buckets (方向③): bootstrap = before the first start_script, script_gap = between scripts, shutdown = after GUT end_run, other = defensive fallback

SEE-1587 line-primary: every block-entry probe carries the attribution block (hit-level edges over the full probe surface); per-test/per-script covered line sets are the primary truth (test_to_lines / script_to_lines / line_to_tests), and file/function views are derived projections from line facts plus the source registry; lane event counts are all-probe events (not comparable to the old fn-entry counts), and the acceptance arm runs the plain template (attribution off by design)
every hit event is counted in exactly one lane/phase; rates use the three-lane sum as denominator — no hit is silently assigned
unattributed_hotspots rank probe sites by unattributed hit events with line and function_id resolution
this is a snapshot of one run bound to recipe_hash; code/test changes make it stale — rebuild periodically
diagnostic evidence only — certification stays full-face (not_certified, exploratory)
